title: Sequence-partitioned attention: interleaved ownership, partials and their stable merge
description: partitioned-attention's ownership (position mod world) and reduction: each rank attends its own rows into a partial with its log normalizer, and the merge of the partials equals attention over the whole sequence. The host form of a long sequence split across devices. Its device form is the technique on one GPU: attention-state's device form with the registry's split-KV reader for decode and verify windows (each row's keys split over KV partitions, piece i to partition i mod P, partials merged by their log-sum-exps, in captured rounds too), its log-sum-exps on request (lse) and merge() for partials from other devices. A captured prompt chunk (prompts:attention) reads the staged prompt table on the device, as softmax-attention's device form does.

world.description: Ranks of the host form's interleaved ownership (position mod world)

page_size.description: Positions per local page of the host form's ranks

partitions.description: KV partitions of the device form's split-KV reader (0: from the GPU's SM count, the KV heads and the page kind); a row's bits depend on it

piece.description: Positions per piece of the split-KV reader (0: the kernel's default from the head width and the page kind); a row's bits depend on it

kernels.description: auto: the registry's paged-kv-attention kernels where they load (FlashInfer for 16-bit and FP8 prompt rows); torch: every row in torch

workspace_mib.description: MiB of partials the split-KV reader allocates when the plugin is made (memory() declares them): a launch reads as many rows as they hold

flashinfer.description: auto: FlashInfer's paged prefill for prompt rows of 16-bit and FP8 pages where it is installed, its workspaces allocated when the plugin is made; off: none (a model whose KV pages FlashInfer cannot read, fp8:row or INT8, allocates nothing for it)

flashinfer_mib.description: MiB of FlashInfer's scheduling workspace, allocated when the plugin is made where FlashInfer serves (memory() declares it with its wrappers' own workspaces)

prompt_reader.description: prefill: prompt rows through a prompt reader (FlashInfer's prefill or the registry's), fastest, another reduction than decode rows' (a scored token may differ from the served one by more than 0.001 nats); decode: prompt rows (a step's and a captured chunk's) in the decode's reduction, the split-KV reader as window rows of up to 64 columns (each program folding its partitions as the merge does) or its torch fallback over the page tables: a scored token equals the same token served, bit for bit, over every page type (window rows through the split-KV reader too, no FlashInfer)

kernels.name: crit-labs/paged-kv-attention
kernels.fallback: each row's partitions merged in a masked FP32 softmax over the pool's page tables in torch, prompt rows by torch's SDPA
